exercises.final: Keep the weekly written status in both approaches. A: replace routine status-sharing meetings with that existing written status and reserve discussion for explicitly flagged decisions or blockers; the existing meeting owner routes each flagged item to its current accountable person. A routine week needs no status meeting; an urgent cross-team issue can fail if nobody owns the response deadline, so confirm that responsibility within existing authority. B: retain a fixed short coordination window but batch agenda items by shared dependency and require the decision needed, not a presentation of status. A routine week resolves related decisions together; an issue arriving immediately after the window can miss a deadline, requiring the existing urgent escalation route. A changes the default from synchronous reporting to exception discussion; B retains synchronous coordination but changes batching and input structure. Neither buys software, removes written status, or presumes new decision rights.
